podcast.title: Producer of Green Day's Dookie
podcast.body: Rob Cavallo produced Green Day's album *Dookie*. He was instrumental in convincing the band to sign with a major label, offering them $300,000 without having ever seen them perform live, and had previously worked with The Goo Goo Dolls, while his father managed Love & Spoonful and Earth, Wind & Fire. "He convinced Green Day that the only way forward was for them to sign with a major label. He'd signed the Goo Goo dolls and his dad had once managed the love and spoonful and earth-winded fire. And after hearing some Green Day, he offered them $300,000. And that was without ever seeing them play live."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Major Label Signing by Rob Cavallo
xref.body: Producer Rob Cavallo convinced Green Day to sign with a major label, a decision that went against the core ethos of the punk culture they emerged from. This controversial move led to the band being banned from some of their usual venues and labeled as "sell-outs" by many Bay Area punks. "He convinced Green Day that the only way forward was for them to sign with a major label. So going against the ethos of the punk culture they had grown up in, Green Day signed. That was a huge risk. And it got them banned from some of the places they used to play. As far as a lot of Bay Area punks were concerned, Green Day was dead to them. There were sell-outs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rapid Recording of Dookie
xref.body: The band completed the recording sessions for their album *Dookie* with producer Rob Cavallo in an exceptionally short period of three weeks. "The group burned through the recording sessions with Cavallo in three weeks."
